desc:
Among all contiguous subarrays of nums whose length is even (2, 4, 6, ...), return the largest sum.

Examples: [1, -2, 3, 4] gives 7 (the subarray [3, 4]); [-5, -1, -2] gives -3 (the subarray [-1, -2]).
hints: Plain Kadane forgets the length. Which extra piece of information must a DP state remember here?
Only the parity of the length matters. Track even[i] and odd[i]: the best sums of subarrays ending at i with an even / odd length (when such a subarray exists).
odd[i] = nums[i] + max(0, even[i-1]) (start fresh or extend an even run). even[i] = odd[i-1] + nums[i]. The answer is the best even[i].
editorial: Adding one element flips the parity of the length, so the states just trade places. For a subarray ending at i with an odd length, either it is the single element [nums[i]], or it extends an even-length subarray ending at i-1. A subarray with an even length must extend an odd-length subarray ending at i-1 (a lone element is odd, so an even run never starts fresh).

Hence odd' = nums[i] + max(0, even) and even' = odd + nums[i], where an even run that does not exist yet counts as minus infinity. The answer is the maximum even over all indices. A prefix-sum alternative: the best even-length sum ending at j is P[j+1] minus the smallest prefix sum at an index of the same parity, apart from j+1 itself. O(n) time, O(1) space.
solution:
def maxEvenLengthSum(nums):
    NEG = float("-inf")
    odd = nums[0]
    even = NEG
    best = NEG
    for x in nums[1:]:
        new_even = odd + x
        new_odd = x + max(0, even)
        even, odd = new_even, new_odd
        best = max(best, even)
    return best
